ecosystem.notes: Amazon does not report GMV or any total value of third-party sales, so measure is null. platformRevenue is the third-party seller services net sales line (what Amazon keeps from sellers: commissions plus fulfillment and shipping fees); it excludes advertising sold to sellers (advertising services $56.214B is a separate line). The 62% unit share is a Q4 2024 quarterly figure (quarters in 2024: 61%, 61%, 60%, 62%; no full-year figure is published) and counts units, not dollars. Both study entries keep value null because the claims are a percentage and a per-seller average ($290,000), not billions. The 60% sales share and $290,000 average are Amazon's own self-published report, not an independent or commissioned study, and the 60% is stated as 'today' (report published May 2025), not as an FY2024 measurement. The same report's 'more than $2.5 trillion' is a 25-year cumulative figure and is not recorded. The release was read from Amazon's IR document CDN (s2.q4cdn.com), linked from ir.aboutamazon.com, which blocked automated access with a Cloudflare challenge.
